original_question: Let p be a prime. A totally imprimitive p-group H of finitary permutations is said to have the cyclic-block property if in the cycle decomposition of every element the support of every cycle is a block for H. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω. Does every transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G contain a transitive subgroup which has the cyclic-block property?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.6 in the "New Problems" section of the current 21st-edition material in arXiv:1401.0300.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official formulation of Problem 21.6 almost verbatim: it fixes a prime p, defines the cyclic-block property exactly as the paper does, places G as a transitive subgroup of FSym(Ω), and asks whether every transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G contains a transitive subgroup with that property.
missing_details: No paper-critical hypothesis is missing; the draft is already extremely close to the notebook's official wording.
For a fully stand-alone formulation, the standard term "block for H" should be spelled out explicitly.
For a fully stand-alone formulation, the specialist term "totally imprimitive" should be defined, since Problem 21.6 uses it without expansion.
The quantifiers can be made fully explicit by naming the transitive Sylow p-subgroup S ≤ G and asking whether there exists a transitive subgroup H ≤ S with the required property.
refined_question: Fix a prime p. Let Ω be a set, let G ≤ FSym(Ω) be a transitive subgroup, and let S be a transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G. Must S contain a transitive subgroup H such that H is a totally imprimitive p-group and, for every h ∈ H, every cycle in the cycle decomposition of h has support a block for H?
justification: The draft is the right target: it is essentially Problem 21.6 itself, not the older Asar problem 17.13 about minimal non-FC-subgroups. So the only real refinement needed is expositional: make the quantifiers explicit and package the sought subgroup as H ≤ S while preserving the exact scope of 21.6.
